newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on weather, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on weather, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures remained broadly lower late Monday in sluggish trade, with forecasts for above-normal Northeast and Midwest weather this week still undermining physical and paper prices.
By 1350 EDT, May sagged 3.6 cents to $2.09 per million British thermal units, while June was still three cents lower at $2.125. Other deferreds were down by one-half to two cents.

"I think this move (lower) is off the forecasts. The shorts are out of the market and the (cold) weather had to break. My guess is sideways to lower until we get some news," said an East Coast trader.
Traders said forecasts for normal to above-normal weather for the Northeast and Midwest this week helped lower expectations for the early-May cash when flows begin Thursday.
But they agreed cooling loads in Texas and the Southwest could temper the bears, adding activity should remain quiet until the first now that most bidweek nomination deadlines have expired.

Technically, traders pegged first support in June at $2.07, with further buying likely at $2.03 and then along the short-term up trendline at about $2.00. Resistance was seen at $2.24 and then at $2.33.

In the cash Monday, May Gulf Coast gas was talked about five cents lower at $2.04-09. May Midcon prices were off a few cents to the low-to-mid $1.90s. New York city gate gas for May also was modestly lower at about $2.40.
NYMEX said 11,401 Hub contracts traded at 1320 EDT.
On KCBT, May was still down 6.5 cents at $1.955, while deferreds were steady to five cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed 0.1 cent to 13.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
